Ayesha (support): Customer hit repeated 500s + timeouts, says Console shows no request/trace. They want a quick checklist of what we need to triage.
Marta (support): TL;DR checklist to ask customer: minimal curl that reproduces the error (mask bearer token), timestamp (UTC), SDK version + platform, region, account/org id (masked ok), any proxy/edge in front, and either a header value for our trace OR a small log snippet containing the span id.
Ayesha (support): Can you paste a copyable curl example we can share? Also quick commands for pulling a trace out of a HAR or proxy log would help.
Liam (eng): Paste this as-is. Keep the token redacted. Also ask customer to include exact response body and response headers if possible.
Liam (eng): ```bash
# minimal reproducible curl (mask token)
curl -v "https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: demo-123" \
  -d '{"input":"short prompt"}'
```
Marta (support): For us, the most useful things to attach: the raw curl output (stdout/stderr), the HTTP response headers (showing any x-redwood-trace or x-request-id), and a HAR export if from browser.
Ayesha (support): If they give a HAR, this jq snippet extracts our trace header quickly:
```bash
jq -r '.log.entries[].request.headers[] | select(.name|ascii_downcase=="x-redwood-trace") | .value' requests.har
```
Liam (eng): If they only have server/proxy logs, ask them to grep for common keys: `x-redwood-trace`, `x-request-id`, `redwood-trace`, or the pattern `trace=`. Example: `grep -i -E "x-?redwood|x-request-id|trace=" access.log | tail -n 200`
Marta (support): Mobile SDK quick tips to surface trace/span: ask them to enable verbose logs and look for lines that include `trace_id` or `span_id`. For Android: `adb logcat | grep Redwood` after setting `Redwood.setLogLevel(Log.DEBUG)`; for iOS: check device console for `RedwoodSDK` entries.
Ayesha (support): If the Console shows a request but no trace, tell them: open Requests -> click the row -> expand Diagnostics/Metadata panel -> copy the string labeled `trace` or `span`. Screenshot of that panel is fine if they can't copy.
Liam (eng): If they can run a quick internal curl, have them set an explicit header so we can correlate quickly: `-H "X-Redwood-Trace: my-check-<ts>"` then provide that exact value. We'll search for it across logs.
Marta (support): What to redact before sending: full bearer tokens, customer PII in payloads. Keep timestamps, header names/values, region, and truncated account id (last 6 chars) so we can map the tenant.
Ayesha (support): Also ask them to include the exact SDK release string (e.g., `redwood-sdk-android 0.9.4` or `redwood-js 1.2.0`) — helps narrow kernel selection differences.
Liam (eng): If they can't reproduce, ask for a network capture snippet (HAR or tcpdump) around the UTC timestamp they saw the error. A 30s window is usually enough.
Marta (support): If they want to generate a debug bundle via Console, tell them: Console -> Help & Support -> Export diagnostics -> include `requests`, `runtime-logs`, `env`. If they can't access the export, bring us the curl + headers at minimum.
SupportBot: :eyes: auto-note: when debug bundle arrives, include thread_ts and add tag `support:trace-handoff` to ticket.
Ayesha (support): OK I'll send this checklist to the customer now. @Liam can you watch for `my-check-` markers in logs for the next 30m?
Liam (eng): On it. :thumbsup:
Marta (support): One more thing — ask the customer to try a tiny payload to rule out payload-size-related timeouts (e.g., `{"input":"hi"}`). If that succeeds but their larger payload fails, mention it here so we can check batching/kv cache paths.
Ayesha (support): Thanks team. I'll update once they reply with attachments.
